newsitem.title: USA: Corning to divest housewares business.
newsitem.headline: Corning to divest housewares business.

text.p: Corning Inc. said Monday it is exploring the sale of its worldwide consumer housewares business, including the Pyrex and Revere Ware brands, in an effort to focus on its communications, environmental and advanced materials units.
Corning has hired Goldman, Sachs & Co. to help with the divestiture, which it hopes to complete by the end of 1997.
"This decision is the latest step in the deliberate implementation of our strategy to concentrate on high-growth, technology-driven businesses," said Corning Chairman Roger Ackerman.

"The financial performance of our consumer products business has improved substantially. However, as we assessed the business relative to our strategic direction, it was apparent that this business was not a clear fit with our areas of concentration."

Corning entered the consumer housewares business with its invention of Pyrex bakeware in 1915 and today manufactures Corelle, Corning Ware, Pyrex, Revere Ware and Visions. The business had 1996 revenues of about $630 million.
The business will operate as usual as the Corning, N.Y.-based company seeks a buyer, it said.
Corning said it would use proceeds from the divestiture to improve its balance sheet and invest in its communications, environmental and advanced materials businesses.

Corning said it has reinvented itself numerous times in the past, creating new businesses such as fiber optics, optical cable, photonic technologies and liquid-crystal-display glass. It completed the spinoff of its health care services businesses last year.

Corning makes optical fiber, optical cable, and photonic components, high-performance glass and components for televisions, advanced materials for the scientific and environmental markets and consumer products.
Corning's stock fell $1.75 to $50.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
